scenario.name: g7-codex-recheck
scenario.description: G7 follow-up (#470): live re-check of risk rows 66 and 73 on the current Codex, by a quarantined client against the running shared daemon. No TUI. Not a gate run; not verdict-bearing.

executableCheck.basis: First-party, verified 2026-10-03 in the three steps listed above. The release zip hashes to the API digest. `gh release verify-asset` confirmed it against the release attestation for tag `v0.9.1` (sha1 `8544776216a8d28088db59a5344ea21ee2d05d2b`). Its `herdr.exe` hashes to this value. The same value is the sha256 of the installed `herdr.exe` (25562624 bytes, standalone package `0.9.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and of the herdr the driver recorded in run `G5-2026-10-02` (`herdr.executable.sha256`).

holders: the shared Codex app-server daemon (left running; the driver never stops it) may hold the directory of a thread it loaded under scratch; it is released on `codex app-server daemon stop`, or when the daemon unloads the thread (documented: no subscribers and no thread activity for 30 minutes). The driver does not call thread/archive or thread/delete, which would unload it sooner, because both write to the operator's Codex thread store (thread/delete destroys the run's rollout) and whether their shutdown releases the directory handle is unverified

row66.claim: items queued before the interrupt wait and run after the next uninterrupted turn
row66.basis: both adds accepted; nothing dispatched in the quiet window; after the next uninterrupted turn the two items ran in separate turns, in order, the second after the first completed

row66.claim: an add to an idle thread whose last turn was interrupted waits until a turn completes uninterrupted
row66.basis: accepted; nothing in the quiet window; ran after the next turn completed

row66.claim: an add to an unloaded thread is accepted and waits; loading the thread dispatches it
row66.basis: accepted; no event and still unloaded through the quiet window; thread/resume then dispatched it

row66.claim: an extra member in thread/queue/add is accepted and ignored
row66.basis: accepted; the message ran as one turn with exactly the text sent

row66.claim: (b) other daemon clients can reorder, update or delete a queued item
row66.basis: update, reorder and delete from a second client were accepted, shown by thread/queue/list, and dispatch followed them (item 3, then item 2 as updated; item 1 never ran)

row73.claim: what the app-server does with an approvalPolicy override on thread/resume, in three states of the thread: loaded and idle with subscribers, loaded and idle with no subscriber, and not loaded (MCPB-CDX-006 asks about a loaded thread; the answer depends on its subscribers)
row73.basis: loaded, idle, with subscribers: NOT-APPLIED; loaded, idle, no subscriber: APPLIED-AND-RETAINED; not loaded (control): APPLIED-AND-RETAINED

loadedWithSubscribers.basis: in this state (loaded, idle, with subscribers) the response reports "on-request", not the override "untrusted"

loadedWithoutSubscribers.basis: in this state (loaded, idle, no subscriber) the response reports the override and a later resume without it reports it too

subscribers.note: p-main, the only connection that held the thread, unsubscribed; no other connection resumed it

unloadedControl.basis: in this state (not loaded (control)) the response reports the override and a later resume without it reports it too

caveats: judged from the wire only: no turn was started after an override, so its effect on a turn is not observed
